review_scope: Publisher-side evidence review of the ollama-llmwatch review. All 46 inventory claim blocks were re-checked against the primary sources listed below and eight figures were corrected before this receipt was signed: (1) PyPI last-month downloads 84 -> 69, last-week 25 -> 14, last-day 0 -> 1, with the as-of date moved to 2026-10-07; (2) Ollama issue #3144 reactions 140 -> 141; (3) toptop stars 17 -> 18; (4) LLMxRay stars ~8 -> ~11; (5) npm llmxray last-month downloads 395 -> ~380; (6) agentacct stars ~758 -> ~766 and tokentelemetry ~374 -> ~376; (7) Ollama/llama.cpp/vLLM star counts refreshed to 182,491/130,606/93,342 and forks to 18,137; (8) two previously unlinked adjacent tools (agentacct, tokentelemetry) were added to the Sources list so every named tool resolves to a primary repository. Unchanged and confirmed: the README-derived board figures (12 req / 18m04s / WAIT 91% / eight minutes of silent reading / 512-token progress cadence / 10x-per-second repaint), the v0.33.3 release date (2026-09-02), the LLMxRay 4375-vs-115 tok/s and 64.6-vs-18.6 ms measurements, the 57.3s-vs-33m29s turn pair (n=6/n=5), the speculative-decoding acceptance table, the M1 Max tok/s table, the PyPI release skew (0.9.1 latest with 0.8.0 never published), and all four cited Ollama tracker issues. The 3.5x and 38x figures are reproduced as the source's own illustration, not as our test.

claims.note: Title and meta description only; 'ollama' is the reviewed product and the description restates the article's own definition, so no external claim is being made.

Repository API on 2026-10-07: MIT license, created 2026-08-16, 4 stars, 0 forks, 0 open issues. 'Created in August 2026' and star count match; PyPI last-month downloads refreshed to 69 (previously 84, an Oct-1 vintage).

Re-read live: issue #3144 titled 'add /metrics endpoint', opened 2024-03-14, state open, 141 reactions (was 140) and 48 comments. PR #16998 opened 2026-07-01 +936/-50 in 13 files, gated by OLLAMA_METRICS; PR #18508 opened 2026-09-17 +407 in 4 files and its body says 'alternative rather than as a replacement'; PR #13901 opened 2026-01-25 with 0 comments and a body calling itself 'a messy proof of concept draft'.

Structural explanation of the request lifecycle (prefill builds the KV cache and emits nothing; generate streams tokens). It describes the documented behaviour of the API surface rather than reporting a measurement.

README 'The problem' section: a coding agent sends 30,000-55,000 tokens per turn; ~eight minutes of silent reading on an M1 Max at 27B while the answer takes about twenty seconds. Sample board header shows 12 req / 18m04s and WAIT 91% of session spent in prefill; all reproduced verbatim from the README.
91% prefill implies 9% generate; arithmetic on the README's own WAIT figure, not an independent measurement.
The slot/task print_timing line is quoted from the README's log-format example (id 0 | task 2313 | n_tokens = 4096, progress = 0.27).

README states the log format is internal with no stability guarantee, mitigated by tests against captured logs under tests/fixtures/*.log; the fixtures directory was confirmed to hold cache-hit.log, mlx-request.log, model-load.log and request-with-progress.log.

Log paths re-checked against Ollama's own troubleshooting page: macOS ~/.ollama/logs/server.log, Linux systemd journalctl -u ollama, container stdout/docker logs, Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%\Ollama\server.log.
README 'Reading the screen' section documents that hints state the conclusion rather than leaving the operator to interpret raw counters.
Hint strings quoted verbatim from the README hint block (cache gone / same prompt 5x / 3 cancels in a row / slow: 2 models loaded, swapping).

README states the server writes a progress line only every 512 tokens (5-10 seconds apart) and that position is projected from the last measured rate and repainted ~10x/second, clamped so the bar cannot claim work that has not happened.

README FAQ: GPU sits pinned near 100% and CPU near idle whether the rate is 13 or 8 tok/s because the bottleneck is memory bandwidth, not compute; the README also notes macOS GPU utilisation needs sudo. The tool therefore reads measured throughput instead.
Section heading naming the Ollama 0.33.3 field; no factual assertion beyond the field's name.

Release-date check: Ollama v0.33.3 published 2026-09-02. The LLMxRay write-up states 0.33.3 added prompt_eval_cached_count to /api/generate and /api/chat and redefined prompt_eval_duration to cover only uncached prompt tokens, while prompt_eval_count still means total prompt size.

LLMxRay table: warm request prompt_eval_count 38, cached 37, duration 8.7 ms gives 4375 tok/s by the old formula against an actual 115 tok/s (38x), with no error or warning. Ollama's api/types.go declares PromptEvalCachedCount *int `json:"...,omitempty"` and its Metrics.Summary() computes uncached = max(0, PromptEvalCount-cached) before dividing, confirming both the nullable-unknown semantics and the internal fix.
LLMxRay: the Anthropic-compatible endpoint's input_tokens now means total minus cached; the same prompt reported 38 cold and 1 warm. Reported as the maintainer's live observation on 0.33.3.
Section heading asserting a 3.5x layout effect; the underlying measurement is carried by the following block.

LLMxRay table: same model and same 324-token system prompt, moving one 21-token timestamp from top to bottom changed prefill from 64.6 ms to 18.6 ms (4 vs 290 reused tokens). The source itself labels the 3.5x ratio an illustration rather than a benchmark, and the article carries that framing.
Section heading; the turn-time figures are carried by the following block.
README --turns output reproduced exactly: qwen3.8:27b-mtp-128k at low effort median 57.3s (n=6), high effort 33m29s (n=5), wall clock including tool time. The article's '35x' is that pair's ratio.
README speculative-decoding section: acceptance is the number that matters because a drafter can cost time; the article's cautionary framing matches the source.
README acceptance table quoted exactly (code/structured 58-81% at 1.5x, rote output/lists 93% at 2x, freeform prose 18% at 0.6x slower than no drafter).
README FAQ tok/s table for an M1 Max: 27B at Q4 10-17, 14B at Q4 25-30, MoE such as Qwen3-30B-A3B much higher because only a fraction of weights are read per token. Described as generation figures.

toptop README: Rust, GPLv3 badge, star count re-read as 18 (article said 17), one small static binary with zero runtime dependencies, self-described 'the local-inference observability layer for your terminal'; auto-discovers vLLM/llama.cpp/Ollama/TGI/TensorRT-LLM/LM Studio and reads llama.cpp/vLLM/TGI Prometheus /metrics plus Ollama /api/ps for prefill and generation tok/s, KV-cache pressure, queue depth and TTFT, tokens/sec/watt, --diagnose 72-column verdict (README shows 'MEMORY-BANDWIDTH BOUND / bandwidth 92% / compute 24%'), Ollama CPU verdicts, Prometheus/JSON export, --serve-metrics default 127.0.0.1:9709, and an SSH multi-host fleet view.

ollama-metrics README: transparent proxy forwarding to Ollama while collecting prompt/generated token totals, request duration, time per token, model memory and load status; pre-built Grafana dashboard; OLLAMA_HOST and PORT configuration; image ghcr.io/norskhelsenett/ollama-metrics. GitHub API shows 42 stars and last push 2025-06-24. The response-time blindness is an inference from the proxy design, and the article states it as such.

LLMxRay API shows Apache-2.0, 11 stars (article said ~8), last push 2026-10-02; npm dl-tags latest v0.6.0 with 379 downloads in the last month (article said 395). Its own article page is the source for the prefill-formula analysis, and it ships live cache-reuse measurement against a running daemon.

agentacct (mikehasa) re-read at 766 stars and tokentelemetry (VasiHemanth) at 376 stars (article said ~758 and ~374), both from repository search. Their READMEs place them in per-task/per-run cost attribution, a different question from per-request latency.
PyPI metadata: requires_python >=3.9, license MIT; README states Python 3.9+ and no dependencies, with uv/pipx install commands and both ollama-llmwatch and llmwatch entry points.
README usage block: --plain, --last, --json, --codex, --log PATH, --history --days, --turns --days, --compare, --export csv, --no-history and --debug-unparsed are all documented flags.

README proxy section: --proxy listens on 8081 and forwards to an OpenAI-compatible server on 8080, aimed at mlx-lm, LM Studio and vLLM, whose logs carry no token counts; llama.cpp is the documented exception and uses --log because its log does carry them.

README limitations: no remote log access, internal log-format dependency, macOS verified while Linux journald and Docker paths are 'written but unverified', Windows unsupported, no GPU/KV/queue view; MLX generation tokens reconstructed from speculative stats. Adoption figures refreshed to 69 last-month / 14 last-week / 1 last-day as of 2026-10-07, and 13 closed / 0 open issues were confirmed via the GitHub API; the release skew below cites PyPI directly.

Repo counts re-read on 2026-10-07: ollama/ollama 182,491 stars and 18,137 forks, ggml-org/llama.cpp 130,606, vllm-project/vllm 93,342. Release dates from the releases API: v0.35.0 2026-09-28 and the v0.40.0-rc0 tag committed 2026-09-25 (prerelease, so not in the stable releases list). Ticket states re-read: #16051 open (MLX bf16 cold prefill 60-400x slower than warm), #18505 open (MLX nvfp4 stall at processed=total-1), #18267 closed (prefix-cache restore truncated to a multiple of 8192, 17-27 s re-prefill), #17829 closed (no MLX prompt caching between requests).
README 'How do I actually make things faster?' lists cutting the agent prompt size first and tuning flags last, matching the article's ordering.
README prompt-caching note that only uncached tokens are computed; the 3.5x figure and the stable-first/volatile-last guidance are the LLMxRay measurement, attributed there.

LLMxRay 'The measurement I got wrong first': each layout must be sent twice, once with its own values and once with them changed, because real traffic repeats one layout with a fresh value; only the second send tests cache survival.
README SYSTEM panel warns on swap and the canonical hint is the two-models-loaded swapping line; the MLX caveat that two resident large models swap is also in the README.
README FAQ recommends a smaller or MoE model for throughput because only a fraction of weights is read per token.
README speculative-decoding section: acceptance can go the wrong way, so it should be measured per workload rather than assumed.
README WAIT line description: 'share of your session spent reading rather than writing', presented as the headline split.
Verdict paragraph restates figures established earlier (stars, refreshed 69-download vintage, macOS verification, release skew, zero dependencies, 13 closed issues); no new claim.

The transferable lesson: the 0.33.3 redefinition over-reported up to 38x, and prompt layout was worth 3.5x in the measured example; both trace to the LLMxRay analysis, with the tool's own cache panel as the local feedback mechanism.
FAQ answer restates MIT license, zero runtime dependencies, Python 3.9+, what the panels show and that it never calls the Ollama API; all covered by the README and PyPI metadata cited above.
FAQ answer: the API emits the first token and a final usage object with nothing between; PR #13901 (2026-01-25) is still open with 0 comments and issue #3144 is still open, re-read on 2026-10-07.

FAQ answer restates the 0.33.3 (2026-09-02) field addition, the redefined duration, the up-to-38x over-report and the corrected formula, matching the LLMxRay write-up and the api/types.go calculation.
